stem: If one of these households that owns at least 2 cars is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting a household that uses public transit for the weekly commute?
stimulus:
A city planning office surveyed 250 households along a proposed light-rail corridor. Each household reported how many cars it owns and whether any member uses public transit for the weekly commute. The results are shown in the table.

Corridor Household Survey
Transit use | 0 cars | 1 car | 2 cars | 3 or more cars | Total
Uses transit | 48 | 36 | 10 | 6 | 100
Does not use transit | 12 | 74 | 50 | 14 | 150
Total | 60 | 110 | 60 | 20 | 250
explanation: "At least 2 cars" includes both the 2-cars column and the 3-or-more column, so you build that group first: $60 + 20 = 80$ households. Of those, $10 + 6 = 16$ use transit. The probability is $\frac{16}{80} = \frac{1}{5}$.

A.why: You found the right count of 16, but you divided by all 250 households, which gives $\frac{16}{250} = \frac{8}{125}$. The condition limits you to the 80 households with at least 2 cars, so 80 is the denominator.

C.why: You divided 16 by the 100 transit users. That gives $\frac{16}{100} = \frac{4}{25}$, which is the fraction of transit users who own at least 2 cars. That's the reverse question. The given group is the households with at least 2 cars.

D.why: You read "at least 2" as "more than 2" and used only the 3-or-more column, which gives $\frac{6}{20} = \frac{3}{10}$. Households with exactly 2 cars also meet the condition, so that column belongs in the group.

stem: If one of these artifacts is selected at random, what is the probability that it is pottery, given that it was not recovered from Trench B?
stimulus:
An excavation team recovered 171 artifacts from four trenches at a site. The table shows the number of artifacts of each material found in each trench.

Artifacts Recovered by Trench and Material
Material | Trench A | Trench B | Trench C | Trench D
Pottery | 26 | 31 | 18 | 22
Bone | 9 | 14 | 12 | 7
Stone | 5 | 10 | 6 | 11
Total | 40 | 55 | 36 | 40
explanation: 'Not from Trench B' means Trenches A, C, and D together. No single printed total covers that group, so you add the column totals: $40+36+40$. The pottery inside that group is $26+18+22$. The probability is $\frac{26+18+22}{40+36+40}$.

A.why: You read 'not from Trench B' as 'from Trench B' and used only that column. The given group is every trench except B.

B.why: You divided by all 171 artifacts, so the condition did nothing. Once you're told the artifact isn't from Trench B, the Trench B artifacts leave the denominator.

C.why: You divided by all the pottery. That gives the probability that a piece of pottery came from somewhere other than Trench B, which swaps the denominator. The group after 'given that' is the artifacts outside Trench B, not the pottery.

stem: If one of these earthquakes is selected at random, what is the probability that it was shallow, given that its magnitude was greater than or equal to 5.0?
stimulus:
A seismic network classified every earthquake it recorded in one year by magnitude and by focal depth. The table shows the proportion of all recorded earthquakes that fall in each category.

Proportion of Recorded Earthquakes by Depth and Magnitude
Depth | Under 4.0 | 4.0 to 4.9 | 5.0 to 5.9 | 6.0 or greater
Shallow | 0.42 | 0.18 | 0.07 | 0.03
Deep | 0.16 | 0.09 | 0.04 | 0.01
explanation: 'Greater than or equal to 5.0' covers two columns: 5.0 to 5.9 and 6.0 or greater. Build that group by adding all four of its cells: $0.07+0.03+0.04+0.01$. The shallow part of the group is $0.07+0.03$. You can treat the proportions as counts, because the overall scale cancels when you divide. The probability is $\frac{0.07+0.03}{0.07+0.03+0.04+0.01}$.

A.why: You used only the 5.0 to 5.9 column. The condition covers both columns at or above 5.0, so the 6.0 or greater column belongs in both the numerator and the denominator.

B.why: You divided by the whole shallow row. That gives the probability that a shallow earthquake had magnitude 5.0 or greater, which reverses the question. The given group is the strong earthquakes, not the shallow ones.

D.why: You read 'greater than or equal to 5.0' as '6.0 or greater' and dropped the 5.0 to 5.9 column. The 'or equal to' brings that boundary column back into the group.

stem: If one of the stars with at least 2 known planets is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting a class G star?
stimulus:
An observatory catalogued 80 nearby stars by spectral class and by the number of planets known to orbit each star.

Stars by Spectral Class and Number of Known Planets
Known planets | Class G | Class K | Total
0 | 14 | 22 | 36
1 | 9 | 12 | 21
2 | 7 | 5 | 12
3 or more | 10 | 1 | 11
Total | 40 | 40 | 80
explanation: The table has no single row for "at least 2," so you build that group yourself. It is the "2" row plus the "3 or more" row: $12 + 11 = 23$ stars. Class G stars in those rows: $7 + 10 = 17$. The probability is $\frac{17}{23}$.

A.why: You found the right numerator, 17, but divided by all 80 stars in the catalogue. The selection is made only from the 23 stars with at least 2 planets.

B.why: You divided by the 40 class G stars. That answers a different question: of the class G stars, what fraction have at least 2 planets? The group being selected from is the stars with at least 2 planets, so that group is the denominator.

C.why: You read "at least 2" as "more than 2" and used only the "3 or more" row. "At least 2" includes stars with exactly 2 planets, so that row belongs in the group too.

stem: If one of the amphibians that was not caught at Pond 2 is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting a spring peeper?
stimulus:
During a wetland survey, ecologists caught and released 120 amphibians at three ponds. The results are shown.

Amphibians Caught by Species and Pond
Species | Pond 1 | Pond 2 | Pond 3 | Total
Green frog | 18 | 30 | 12 | 60
Spring peeper | 30 | 10 | 20 | 60
Total | 48 | 40 | 32 | 120
explanation: "Not caught at Pond 2" means Pond 1 and Pond 3 together: $48 + 32 = 80$ amphibians. Spring peepers in those two ponds: $30 + 20 = 50$. The probability is $\frac{50}{80} = \frac{5}{8}$.

A.why: You used Pond 2 itself, $\frac{10}{40}$, and missed the word "not." The group is every pond except Pond 2.

C.why: You built the right group of 80, but you counted the green frogs in it, $\frac{30}{80}$. The question asks for spring peepers.

D.why: You counted the 50 spring peepers outside Pond 2 but divided by all 120 amphibians. Only the 80 amphibians not caught at Pond 2 can be selected.

stem: If one of the prints in drawer 3 or higher is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting a linocut?
stimulus: A printmaking studio stores its work in a flat file with 9 numbered drawers. Drawers 1 through 4 each hold 15 prints, and all of them are linocuts. Drawers 5 through 9 each hold 12 prints: 4 linocuts and 8 etchings.
explanation: Build the group by multiplying drawers by prints per drawer. Drawers 3 and 4 hold $2 \times 15 = 30$ prints, all linocuts. Drawers 5 through 9 hold $5 \times 12 = 60$ prints, of which $5 \times 4 = 20$ are linocuts. That makes $30 + 60 = 90$ prints, and $30 + 20 = 50$ of them are linocuts. The probability is $\frac{50}{90} = \frac{5}{9}$.

A.why: You read "drawer 3 or higher" as "higher than drawer 3" and left drawer 3 out. That gives $\frac{15 + 20}{15 + 60} = \frac{35}{75}$. Drawer 3 is part of the group.

B.why: You built the right group of 90, but you counted the 40 etchings in it instead of the linocuts.

D.why: You counted the 50 linocuts in drawers 3 through 9 but divided by all 120 prints in the flat file. Only the 90 prints in drawer 3 or higher can be selected.
